what: Issue #92 acceptance-condition-4 profile-only compute-path decomposition for block circular-buffer buffering
scope_note: This record is diagnostic-only. It is not a throughput headline and does not replace any prior measurement record.

toolchain.device_profiler_environment: TT_METAL_DEVICE_PROFILER unset; fixed release image cycle-counter transport used

labels.block_external_input_cb_wait: profiled cb_wait_front for R/X0 input CBs only
labels.block_external_output_cb_wait: profiled cb_wait_front for external output CBs; zero when compute does not wait on output
labels.block_external_input_cb_reserve: profiled cb_reserve_back for R/X0 input CBs; zero when reader owns input reserves
labels.block_external_output_cb_reserve: profiled cb_reserve_back for external output CBs
labels.unclassified_overhead: total profile interval minus all named sections; not a measured busy share

instrumentation.disabled_path: profile=false keeps the existing non-profile block calls and does not allocate profile CBs; board-free source/schema tests cover this contract.

commands.batch8192_capture: TT_METAL_WATCHER=1 HEKATUS_TT_IMAGE=<fixed-release-image> HEKATUS_TT_CONTAINER_TIMEOUT_S=60 timeout 60s ./enodia/tt/bench/run_in_container.sh <out-dir> -- --device-id 0 --only newton_schulz_L{16|32}_b8192 --dtype bfloat16 --memory l1 --kind custom_newton_schulz --custom-variant bf16-fp32state --custom-math-fidelity HiFi3 --fuse-s --matrix-block 4 --input-memory l1 --r-memory l1 --x0-memory l1 --profile [--double-buffer] --iters 1 --repeats 1

interpretation.evidence_level: supported decomposition; exact source semantics rule out treating DEST brackets as hardware wait durations

source_audit.scope: Exact v0.75.0 tt-metal source tree used for the audit; tt_metal/tt-llk is bundled in that tree rather than a separate git submodule at this revision.

tile_regs_acquire.math_helper: tt_metal/tt-llk/tt_llk_blackhole/llk_lib/llk_math_common.h:93-98 calls math_dest_wait without a RISC-V polling loop.
tile_regs_acquire.hardware_wait: tt_metal/tt-llk/tt_llk_blackhole/common/inc/cmath_common.h:262-265 implements math_dest_wait with TTI_SEMWAIT on semaphore MATH_PACK and STALL_ON_MAX.
tile_regs_acquire.instruction_path: tt_metal/tt-llk/tt_llk_blackhole/common/inc/ckernel_ops.h:474-478 defines TT_OP_SEMWAIT and TTI_SEMWAIT; :12 defines INSTRUCTION_WORD as .ttinsn inline assembly. common_globals.h:15-28 selects the MATH/PACK body for the corresponding TRISC build.
tile_regs_acquire.semantics: The math-side API emits a hardware semaphore-wait instruction through the TRISC instruction stream; it does not poll the semaphore in RISC-V code.

tile_regs_wait.pack_helper: tt_metal/tt-llk/tt_llk_blackhole/llk_lib/llk_pack_common.h:24-27 implements llk_packer_wait_for_math_done with TTI_SEMWAIT on semaphore MATH_PACK and STALL_ON_ZERO.
tile_regs_wait.instruction_path: The same ckernel_ops.h:474-478 TTI_SEMWAIT and :12 INSTRUCTION_WORD path emits the pack-side hardware wait.
tile_regs_wait.semantics: The pack-side API emits a hardware semaphore-wait instruction; it does not poll the semaphore in RISC-V code.

cb_wait_front.semantics: cb_wait_front reads pages_acked and pages_received_ptr, then executes a RISC-V do/while loop whose reg_read repeats until enough pages are received. This is RISC-V-side polling. The neighboring non-blocking cb_pages_available_at_front at :440-447 likewise directly reads the counter, but does not wait.
cb_wait_front.boundary: The TRISC external-input CB brackets therefore measure the RISC-V polling call interval, unlike the tile_regs_* brackets, which surround instruction emission for a hardware wait.

evidence: For L32 batch8192, TRISC0 external input CB wait falls from 45.004% one-window to 6.303% two-window; for L16 it falls from 45.195% to 10.106%.

The other TRISC external-input wait percentages are already below 0.27% in the batch8192 captures, and external output reserves are below 0.071%; no compute-side external-output CB waits or input reserves were observed.
Because the exact v0.75.0 cb_wait_front source is a RISC-V polling loop, this reduction is evidence for a reduced block-boundary polling/serialization component.

The raw per-TRISC dest_acquire_wait and dest_pack_wait cycle fields are preserved, but their brackets surround calls that emit TTI_SEMWAIT instructions; they do not measure the duration of the hardware-side MATH_PACK semaphore wait.

The raw percentages must therefore be described as RISC-V-side enqueue/dispatch intervals around tile_regs_acquire/tile_regs_wait, not as small hardware handoff waits and not as evidence that DEST handoff is non-dominant.

The prior official counter record provides direct semaphore-wait evidence: Semaphore Zero Wait T2 is approximately 74.69-74.88% one-window and 70.53-70.74% two-window; Semaphore Full Wait T1 is approximately 22.16-22.36% one-window and 25.84-26.06% two-window. These values are relevant to handoff/backpressure waiting, but their kernel-operation phase identity remains unresolved.
TRISC0 residual is approximately 54-89% depending on window and L; TRISC1/TRISC2 residual is approximately 99% because the named accounting covers only the specified brackets.

Residual includes all remaining kernel work and may include hardware instruction-queue backpressure or stop time after an emitted wait; these cycle counters cannot split that time by phase or call it a measured busy percentage without kernel-internal zones.
The official Semaphore Zero Wait T2 and Semaphore Full Wait T1 values above are direct performance-counter evidence of semaphore waiting in both modes, unlike the tile_regs_* RISC-V call brackets.
The semaphore definitions do not identify a unique kernel operation or TRISC phase in this record, and no new semaphore counters were collected in the fixed-image cycle-counter run.

interpretation.conclusion: Two-window buffering removes a large TRISC0 external-input CB polling component for both L16 and L32, supporting reduced block-boundary I/O/compute serialization. The DEST acquire/pack fields are RISC-V-side enqueue/dispatch brackets rather than hardware wait durations, so they cannot establish a small or non-dominant intra-core handoff. Official semaphore waits are the direct handoff-wait evidence, but phase mapping remains incomplete. Residual work remains unclassified and may include hardware instruction-queue backpressure; exact phase causality is insufficient without kernel-internal zones.

limitations: The fixed release image has no Tracy device profiler; this record uses the repository's L1 cycle-counter profile transport and explicitly does not claim Tracy evidence.
The batch4 validation runner reports finite output and profile-page consistency but is not a correctness oracle; prior Watcher correctness records remain authoritative.
External CB counters classify only R/X0 input CB IDs and external output CB IDs; state/intermediate CB operations remain in residual work.

The DEST fields bracket tile_regs_* calls that enqueue hardware semaphore waits, so they do not expose hardware-side wait duration; residual may include instruction-queue backpressure or stop time that these brackets cannot attribute.
Official semaphore waits provide direct synchronization evidence but do not uniquely map to a kernel operation or phase in this capture.
The prior Watcher-plus-profiler overflow, power-off PCIe incident, diagnostic-only qualification, and prior raw measurement records remain unchanged.
